text:
nina: throwing a compact experiment idea: measure speculative decode behaviour when we vary temperature and quant mode together. low-cost perf wins might hide quality regressions at higher temp. thoughts?

oscar: interesting. how do you propose pairing?

nina: matrix: temps = [0.0, 0.7, 1.2], quant builds = [fp16, int8-static, qkv-tail]. for each cell do control (no-spec) vs spec(beam=2, cutoff=0.05). replay same seed/order. capture per-token logprobs, entropy, and top-k jump occurrences (where speculator picks token different from baseline top1).

maya: capture top-k jump frequency is good. also track downstream task accuracy variance vs temp. high temp likely amplifies differences.

ravi: add a small human triage set for outputs where top-k jump + high entropy coincide. that's our hallucination risk bucket.

nina: agreed. acceptance rules: if primary metric drop >0.6pp at any temp with BH-corrected p<0.05, mark cell fail. if perf improvement >15% and no significant quality loss, candidate for canary.

eoscar: tooling: we'll feed this through the replay harness, store artifacts under s3://redwood-infer-experiments/spec-temp-sweep/{build}/{temp}/{ts}/ and attach a short CSV with per-request flags for top-k-jump, entropy, fallback.

eval-bot: queued run launched: s3://redwood-infer-experiments/spec-temp-sweep/6161616161/
eval-bot: quick preview after warmup: int8-static@0.7 spec reduces p95 by 20% but increases top-k-jump rate from 2.1% -> 3.9%; sample triage set created (n=150).
